title: Next-boundary accepted-storage memory versus current River-forcing forecast separation

sequencing.rationale: Freeze the corrected t=24 allocation oracle before observing the zero-storage causality control.

pending_causality.use: execution dependency only; no H5 observed output used to retune frozen H6 references

derivation: The accepted t=24 Basin level from DUMMY-20H contains 7.9903723811 m3 storage above the priority-1 level target of 1.0 m.
At the next allocation boundary the LevelDemand target can release that accepted storage memory, so the no-River root allocation is 32 + 7.9903723811 = 39.9903723811 m3/day.
The next active-River forcing derived from DUMMY-20G is q = 15.999829335153766 * (1.000007990372381 - 0.5) = 8.0000425122 m3/day.
If alpha remains free, the H3/H4 mechanism predicts alpha=0, preserving the 39.9903723811 m3/day root allocation while the accepted storage draw remains visible.
If alpha is diagnostically fixed to one, the same current forcing reduces the root allocation to 39.9903723811 - 8.0000425122 = 31.9903298689 m3/day.
hypotheses: Accepted physical Basin storage memory from day 1 is visible to the next fixed allocation solve through the LevelDemand target.
Current active-River forcing and accepted storage memory have asymmetric allocation semantics: memory remains admitted while the current forcing can be attenuated by the LP low_storage_factor.
Adding current River forcing with alpha free does not change the corrected next-boundary root allocation from the no-River elevated-state control.
Fixing alpha to one reduces that allocation by approximately the full current River forcing.

The invalidated DUMMY-20I premise is corrected: t=0 active forcing is not subtracted directly from source availability, but accepted physical storage memory can still raise the next-boundary allocation prospectively.
